Order 
This fourth bail application under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 has been filed by the applicant for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.559/2022 dated 23.12.2022 registered at Police Station Civil Lines, District Harda (M.P.). for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5(L),6 of the POCSO Act, 2012.

entities.text: Police Station Civil Lines, District Harda
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Applicant is in detention since 23.12.2022.
2.

Applicant's first bail application was dismissed for want of prosecution vide order dated 18.07.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.13766/2023 while his second and third bail applications were dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide orders dated 25.10.2023 and 14.05.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.Nos.47480/2023 and M.Cr.C.No.12691/2024 respectively.
3. As per the prosecution story, prosecutrix developed friendship with the applicant on Instagram and thereafter they started to chat with each other.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17300 2 MCRC-7774-2025
On 22.12.2022, applicant came to Harda and took prosecutrix with him on the pretext of entering into wedlock with her.
Thereafter in Akola they established physical relations.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
He and prosecutrix were having consensual sexual relations.
It is contended that prosecutrix on her own had gone with him.
Prosecutrix has already been examined before the Trial Court and in para-6 of her evidence she has admitted that she had consensually established physical relations with the applicant.
Applicant is in jail for more than 2 years and 04 months and trial is not completed yet.
Therefore, it is prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed grant of bail on the ground that prosecutrix was below 18 years of age and DNA report is positive.
5. In this case prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial court.
Now there is no possibility of influencing of prosecution witnesses and tempering with the prosecution evidence.

Therefore, having taken into consideration the detention period of the applicant and all the facts and circumstances of the case including the fact that final conclusion of the trial will take considerable time, I deem it a fit case for grant of bail.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 483 of the BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17300 3 MCRC-7774-2025 6.

It is directed that applicant - Akshay Bakode be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.100,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with two solvent sureties of 50,000-50,000/-
each to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS,
2023.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE MKL Akshay Bakode vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55619601/
